items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: Lawrence Doey on the clarinet, Sidney Bache clarinet... That was a very fine organization

ctx.x: Well, before you joined that, can you tell us some more about that band? You played with Roy Palmer and...

Well, Roy Palmer, that was Lewis, I mean, Lawrence Doey's band. Lil Hardin Armstrong on the piano, and Lawrence Doey on the clarinet, Sidney Bache clarinet, Bab Frank piccolo, and Sugar Johnny, cornet, and Toby Halls on the drum. That was a very fine organization, very, very good.
What kind of part did the Bab Frank play on the piccolo? I always wondered.

items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: When you had Bache and Lawrence Dewey both... No. Bache were playing clarinet at the time... he played the soprano... he took up the soprano in 1918.

ctx.x: I'm going to ask some more about that other first band we were talking about. When you had Bache and Lawrence Dewey both, did they both play clarinet or did Bache use the soprano sound?

No. Bache were playing clarinet at the time. And one of the best clarinet players ever left New Orleans or anybody's place. Because he, still today, I just heard him in Paris and I'm telling you, he's Mr. Paris. But he played the soprano. And right today, he played better clarinet than the average clarinet player. But he devoted his time with the soprano. He took up the soprano in 1918. And he wanted to play soprano. He played anything with a reed on it. He played. And he, the first fellow I heard, made a one…
